arguments.name: Alexander’s conditional cortical-exclusion and veridical-detail argument
arguments.position: Strongest developed defender, reconstructed without endorsing premises
premises: Severe illness and alleged cortical incapacity are offered to exclude brain production.
Specific faces and later photo recognition are offered as corroboration.
bridge_principles: Accurate retrospective placement coincides with independently measured exclusion of the processes required by the targeted model.
Relevant information was unavailable through ordinary routes.
arguments.conclusion: Conditional pressure on a specified brain-production account; unconditional survival/creator conclusion not established.
arguments.strongest_objection: A-P2T15-002: timing, residual/recovering function and information-access bridges are unverified.
arguments.strongest_reply: AppendixB and Mays appeal to severity, elaborate interactive recall, recovery phenomenological contrast and corroborative testimony; these deserve inspection.
unresolved_issues: No continuous neural measurement; no whole-experience time lock; no blinded pre-photo record.
Even brain independence would not establish timelessness, same-person survival, universal ground or perfect goodness.

arguments.name: Underdetermination of cause and time
arguments.position: Serious direct criticism plus author audit of evidence limits
premises: Dittrich reports responsiveness/sedation; underlying interview disputed.
The clinical reviewers cannot partition illness and drug effects.
Memoir itself limits most temporal simultaneity to conjecture.
bridge_principles: Excluding a mechanism requires relevant synchronized evidence; inability to provide one settled ordinary mechanism does not establish another.
arguments.conclusion: Specific ordinary and nonordinary causes remain underdetermined.
arguments.strongest_objection: A-P2T15-001: exceptionally severe impairment and matching details might challenge ordinary production if independently established.
arguments.strongest_reply: Retain those positive reports, distinguish absence of accessible evidence from evidence of absence, and state exactly which timing/function/acquisition tests remain unmet.
unresolved_issues: No diagnosis of hallucination/fraud from this audit.
Other critic chains, original tapes/charts and historical webpage snapshots uninspected.

arguments.name: Mays’s actual reply to a solely pharmacological account
arguments.position: Narrow direct reply with later clinical comparison
premises: Mays rejects sedation alone and cites Wade plus attributed Potter context.
Memoir acknowledges both illness and sedative use.
Clinical review reports pre-sedation impairment but uncertain later mixture.
bridge_principles: Illness and treatment may jointly affect responsiveness; contextual journalism cannot by itself settle physiology.
arguments.conclusion: Drug-only dismissal is unsupported by this packet; rejecting it does not prove a cortex-free experience.
arguments.strongest_objection: Potter statement is mediated, removed at request, and unsupported by original tape; memoir timing/clinical figures differ.
arguments.strongest_reply: Wade’s separately signed account and published record-review account strengthen illness attribution but retain the causal/timing limits.
unresolved_issues: No wholesale validation of Mays’s final metaphysical assurance.
Mays79–84 fully read as rhetoric/career context; original video/legal materials not authenticated.
